history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE (verify): this file documents the Laxmi/Mahalaxmi temple at Ganapati Peth, Sangli (416416), which sits within/near the Ganpati Mandir complex area - a local city temple. It is NOT the famous Kolhapur Mahalaxmi Shakti Peetha (~45 km away). TripHobo's description calls it 'one of the major shaktipeethas', which appears to be text borrowed from the Kolhapur temple - flag as suspect. A Justdial listing also shows a 'Shri Mahalaxmi Temple' at Tuljainagar, Sangli - whether this is the same shrine or a different one is unverified. The presiding murti is of Goddess Lakshmi, described as carved with precious stones and gold, with a stone lion (her vahana) behind it, plus other deities in the premises. UNVERIFIED: no reliable source found for the temple's founding date, builder, or history.

name: Mahalaxmi Temple
town_description: Sangli is a city on the banks of the Krishna river in western Maharashtra and the district headquarters. It was the capital of the Patwardhan princely state before merger into the Indian Union in 1948, and is famous for its turmeric and jaggery trade. Together with Miraj and Kupwad it forms the Sangli-Miraj-Kupwad municipal corporation.

travel.airport: Kolhapur Airport is the nearest airport (~50-55 km - verify); Pune Airport ~237 km; Mumbai ~390 km.
travel.railway: Sangli Junction and Miraj Junction are the city's two major stations (~5-9 km from Ganapati Peth - verify).
travel.road: Well connected by MSRTC and private buses from Pune, Mumbai, Kolhapur and Goa; the temple is in Ganapati Peth in the city centre.
